followup_explanation:
This is a straightforward academic summarization/explanation task — historical content about civil rights, voting rights, and non-violent protest tactics. There's nothing harm-adjacent, hostile, or distasteful about it, so neither model's moderation-oriented preference profile is relevant here.

Given that, I routed on raw capability. Petrel-235B leads across every benchmark and internal eval that matters for this task: it scores higher on Summarization (83.7 vs 80.3), Extraction & Retrieval (84.8 vs 81.6), and notably MMLU-Pro (80.9 vs 74.8) and IFEval (90.9 vs 85.6). The IFEval gap is meaningful here because the query has specific instruction constraints ("one paragraph," "don't ramble," synthesize multiple sources). Petrel's stronger instruction-following and synthesis capability make it the better fit, with no behavioral downside since the content is benign.
